extracted.intended_audience: journalists and general readers following Korean War armistice/truce negotiations
extracted.subtask_description: Wire-service news coverage of Korean armistice/prisoner-exchange talks, summarizing negotiation procedures, sources, tactical moves, and battlefield developments. Focuses on secrecy, procedural proposals (ports, inspection commissions), and the single sticking point (repatriation rights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential/off-the-record talks to break deadlock
rubrics_metrics.description: IF THE TALKS ARE SHIELDED FROM WORLD OPINION, THEY CAN JUGGLE POSSIBLE COMPROMISES FREELY AND PERHAPS CRACK THE EXHAUSTING DEADLOCK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allied negotiators proposed secret or quasi-confidential executive sessions so negotiators could speak freely; shielding talks from public scrutiny is presented as a tactic to facilitate compromise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial news blackout for preliminary prisoner talks
rubrics_metrics.description: AS A PRELIMINARY STEP THE ALLIED COMMAND ORDERED AN IMMEDIATE PARTIAL NEWS BLACKOUT ON THE PRISONER TALKS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blackout was intended to keep preliminary discussions off the record; only the final agreement (or lack of one) would be announced. The blackout could be conditional (see related metric about lifting it).

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for lifting news blackout—no propaganda conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: COMMAND WARNED THE REDS THAT THE BLACKOUT WOULD BE LIFTED IMMEDIATELY IF THE COMMUNISTS ATTEMPT TO CONVERT THE CONFIDENTIAL TALKS INTO PROPAGANDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The secrecy arrangement is conditional: if one side abuses confidentiality for propaganda, the protective news restriction would be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-the-record executive sessions to permit frank discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: U.N. NEGOTIATORS FELT PRELIMINARY DISCUSSIONS CONCERNING OFF-THE-RECORD SESSIONS SHOULD 'BE FOR THE TIME BEING AT LEAST IN A QUASI'CONFIDENTIAL'... THE U.N. COMMAND SAID NEGOTIATORS WOULD BE ABLE TO SPEAK FREELY IN AN EXECUTIVE SESSION SINCE THEIR REMARKS WOULD NOT BE AIRED IN THE PRESS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit endorsement of off-the-record executive sessions so negotiators can explore compromises without public pressure; implies restricting press access and records temporarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limiting press attendance and release of record portions
rubrics_metrics.description: NEWSMEN NEVER HAVE BEEN ALLOWED TO ATTEND AND ONLY PORTIONS OF THE 'RECORD' HAVE BEEN OPENED TO CORRESPONDENTS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice of barring journalists from sessions and selectively releasing portions of the official record; places emphasis on official spokesmen and communiques as primary public sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prisoner repatriation policy—voluntary vs forced
rubrics_metrics.description: THE ALLIES WANT PRISONERS TO HAVE THE RIGHT TO DECIDE WHETHER THEY SHALL GO BACK HOME. THE REDS DEMAND FORCED REPATRIATION... WHETHER PRISONERS SHOULD BE GIVEN THE RIGHT TO REJECT REPATRIATION. THIS IS THE ONLY ISSUE BLOCKING AGREEMENT ON PRISONER EXCHANGE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the substantive legal/policy sticking point for prisoner-exchange talks: voluntary repatriation (Allies) versus forced repatriation (Reds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive statement exchange as negotiation tactic
rubrics_metrics.description: THE ALLIES MADE THE FIRST MOVE TO BREAK THE DEADLOCK... THEY HANDED THE REDS A 'SUBSTANTIVE STATEMENT' ON THE ISSUE; THE REDS, AFTER A HALF HOUR RECESS, MADE A PRELIMINARY REPLY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negotiators exchange written substantive proposals and take recesses to consider them — a portrayed effective procedural tactic for moving talks forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and approval of ports of entry with detailed maps
rubrics_metrics.description: THE TRUCE STAFF OFFICERS... MAY PUT THE SEAL OF APPROVAL ON DETAILED MAPS OF 10 PORTS OF ENTRY... THE MAPS SHOW SPECIFIC AREAS SUCH AS AIRPORTS AND DOCK FACILITIES WHERE NEUTRAL INSPECTION TEAMS WOULD OPERATE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed, map-based specification of ports (including facilities) is a precondition for moving to other truce-policing issues; acceptance of maps allows progress in negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ports chosen must serve allied troop and supply flow
rubrics_metrics.description: THE REDS STILL ARE CONSIDERING U.N. MAPS OF PUSAN, KANGNUNG, KUNSAN, INCHON AND TAEGU — THE PORTS THROUGH WHICH ALLIED TROOPS AND SUPPLIES WOULD FLOW DURING AN ARMISTICE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Port selection is to be evaluated on their logistical role during armistice (troop/supply flow), not just geographic or political considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral observers at ports to check truce conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: PORTS OF ENTRY WHERE NEUTRAL NATION OBSERVERS CAN CHECK TRUCE CONDITIONS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes a requirement for neutral-nation inspection teams to monitor compliance at specified entry points as part of truce supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and composition of nominations to inspection commission
rubrics_metrics.description: PROPOSAL THAT THE NATIONS' NOMINATIONS BE CUT FROM THREE TO TWO BY EACH SIDE; COMMUNIST NOMINATION OF SOVIET RUSSIA TO A NEUTRAL INSPECTION COMMISSION.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negotiations include adjustments to the number of nominees per side and dispute over whether Soviet Russia may be named to a supposedly neutral commission — both affect perceived neutrality and balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allied demand to ban military airfield construction
rubrics_metrics.description: AN ALLIED DEMAND FOR A BAN ON MILITARY AIRFIELD CONSTRUCTION.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of policing the truce, Allies seek prohibitions on new military airfields to limit rearmament or offensive capabilities during armistice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on official spokesmen and communiqués for public information
rubrics_metrics.description: NEWS OF THE NEGOTIATIONS HAS COME FROM OFFICIAL SPOKESMEN, THE DELEGATES THEMSELVES AND FROM THE OFFICIAL U.N. COMMAND COMMUNIQUE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With journalists excluded, public reporting depends on official statements and communiqués; implies reduced independent verification and a narrower flow of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism toward enemy/propaganda radio claims
rubrics_metrics.description: PEIPING RADIO... SAID RED ANTI-AIRCRAFT CREWS SHOT DOWN 386 ALLIED AIRCRAFT BETWEEN FEB. 1 AND MARCH 10... THE RADIO, OFTEN GIVEN TO EXAGGERATION, SAID THE FIGURES WERE INCOMPLETE REPORTS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises caution when using adversary broadcasts as sources — treat large claimed figures and sensational claims skeptically and note possible exaggeration or incompleteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Session scheduling and adjournment as negotiation tools
rubrics_metrics.description: THE PRISONERS EXCHANGE TALKS WERE POSTPONED FOR THREE HOURS... THERE WAS NO EXPLANATION. THE SESSION ADJOURNED AT 5:10 P.M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of postponements, recesses and adjournments are normal procedural measures in the talks and can be tactical; reporters should note these as part of negotiation dynamics.
